idiom_name: facade with private worker methods; public_send (never send) for mediated dispatch
implementation_notes: Ruby's visibility is enforced by the interpreter but deliberately escapable: private and protected forbid an explicit receiver, yet send reaches private methods, while public_send is documented as calling public methods only - that pair is the mediation lever. The idiomatic realization is a facade object that holds the resource, exposes a small set of public methods that run the policy check, and keeps the workers private; a dispatcher whose method name comes from input uses public_send against an allow-list, never send. The classic wrapper is still written by hand (Forwardable or SimpleDelegator make the forwarding cheap), and in-process mediation remains advisory with respect to code that may use reflection - instance_variable_get, Method#unbind, define_method - so it mediates cooperating code, not an attacker.
code_sketch:
class Vault
  def initialize(store, policy) = (@store, @policy = store, policy)
  def read(subject, id)
    raise SecurityError, "denied: #{id}" unless @policy.allows?(subject, id)
    fetch(id)                    # private: not callable with an explicit receiver
  end
  def dispatch(op, subject, id)  # op comes from input: mediated dispatch only
    public_send(op, subject, id) # never send - send would reach private methods
  end
  private
  def fetch(id) = @store.get(id)
end
pitfalls: send (and __send__) bypasses visibility entirely; any dispatch that calls send on caller-influenced input defeats the facade - use public_send behind an allow-list.
instance_variable_get/instance_variable_set, Method#unbind, remove_method and reopening the class (monkey patching) all reach or replace the mediator at runtime.
protected is not a weaker private that is safe to ignore: it permits an explicit receiver inside the same class hierarchy, which is easy to misread as an authorization decision.
Copying the resource out (dup, clone, to_h on the record) leaves the caller with a reference the mediator cannot revoke.
